If we can easily fit a model that can't be fit in Jags/Bugs, we should write it up (including that Jackman quote)!
A

On Jun 22, 2013, at 12:59 PM, Jeffrey Arnold wrote:

These models came up in an old stan-dev thread. They are just the continuous analog of the HMMs with normal transition and observation distributions, and using the Kalman filter for the forward pass. Here's a link to the intro paper of a special issue of the Journal of Statistical Software from 2011 which reviews software implementations: http://www.jstatsoft.org/v41/i01/paper.

It would be a nice feature for Stan to have, because these models effectively cannot be estimated in BUGS/JAGS E.g. Jackman Bayesian Analysis for the Social Sciences, p 477

It is well known that it is extremely inefficient to sample from
the conditional distributions of each ξt , t = 1, . . . , T − 1, given its neighbors in
the DAG representation of the model (e.g. ξt−1 is a parent of ξt which is a parent
of ξt+1 , and so on). For this reason, this class of model is usually best handled not
in general purpose computer programs for MCMC-based Bayesian analysis such
as WinBUGS or JAGS. That is, these programs parse each ξt as a distinct node
in the DAG representation of the state-space model. My experience is that tens
to hundreds of millions of iterations – taking several days of CPU time on even
fast desktop computers – are required so as to satisfactorily explore the posterior
density for problems with large T using WinBUGS or JAGS. Because temporally
proximate components of the state vector ξ are so highly correlated with another,
it is far more effective to sample from their joint distribution en bloc.

Questions about your comments

You can workaround this because promotion is defined recursively
by a base case

 promote_args(T)::type = ...

and an inductive case:

promote_args(T1,T2,...) =def= promote_args(T1, promote_args(T2,...))

So you can just break 7 apart into:

promote_args<T1, promote_args<T2,....,T7>::type>::type

and |function_signatures::add| only supports up to 5 args.

Would it make sense to write a version of promote_args that supports
a larger number of args?

Also propto only supports up to 6 args. Could I rewrite the template
to support more args?

  • It only supports constant system matrices |F|, |G|, |V|, and |W| because time-varying arguments would require
    defining the function for vectors of matrices and I didn't see any other functions that have done that.
    The right data structure in Stan for this is an array of
    matrices, e.g.,

    parameters {
    matrix[M,N] A[K];
    ...

creates a K-dimensional array of MxN matrices. The way to
write it in signatures would be matrix[], by analogy to
the way an ordinary real array is written real[] in the doc.

In C++, this is just:

std::vector<Eigen::Matrix<T, Eigen::Dynamic, Eigen::Dynamic> > A;

You have to be careful with this kind of implementation because you
don't want to copy matrices if you don't have to.

That's what I've been doing in my Stan code version of these models.
Right now I use a templating system to create CPP macros (for each
combination of matrix and arrays of matrices for each argument) to
create the Stan code.

In function_signatures.hpp what the signature of a function that
takes an array of matrices look like? Does a 1D array of matrices use
expr(MATRIX_T,i)? And to support matrix and 1D array of matrices
I'd add

std::vector<expr_type> matrix_vector_types;
int_vector_types.push_back(MATRIX_T);                  // scalar
int_vector_types.push_back(expr_type(MATRIX_T,1U));    // std vector

Within the function, would this be where I'd use seq_view?
